setup: Stand upright holding a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs with an overhand or neutral grip.
Set your feet hip-width apart and unlock your knees slightly.
Pull your shoulders back and brace your core, maintaining a neutral spine.
steps: Initiate the movement by pushing your hips backward while keeping a soft bend in your knees.
Lower the dumbbells close along the front of your legs until you feel a strong stretch in your hamstrings, typically around mid-shin level.
Reverse the movement by driving your hips forward and contracting your glutes to return to a fully upright standing position.
instructions.breathing: Inhale and brace your core before descending, and exhale as you extend your hips back to the starting position.
cues: Push your hips straight back to the wall behind you.
Keep the dumbbells skimming your legs.
Maintain soft knees without turning it into a squat.

common_faults.fault: Rounding the lumbar spine to reach lower.
common_faults.correction: Stop descending when your hips stop moving backward; depth is dictated by hamstring flexibility, not by touching the floor.

common_faults.fault: Excessive knee bend turning the movement into a squat.
common_faults.correction: Keep the knee angle fixed throughout the descent and focus purely on hip displacement.

common_faults.fault: Allowing the dumbbells to drift away from the legs.
common_faults.correction: Engage your lats to keep the dumbbells pulled tight against your thighs and shins.

precautions: Avoid hyperextending your lower back at the top of the movement.

name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
summary: A bilateral hip-hinge variation performed with dumbbells that emphasizes the hamstrings and glutes through an extended eccentric range.
